newsitem.title: USA: 3M says wins favorable breast implant ruling.
newsitem.headline: 3M says wins favorable breast implant ruling.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co (3M) said an Albuquerque, N.M. jury found in favor of the company in five of six issues relating to a breast-implant case.
After 10-1/2 hours of deliberation, the jury decided 3M should not be held liable for allegations by the plaintiff that her breast implants caused her to have health problems.
But the company said the jury found 3M liable with regard to the design of the plaintiff's implants, and awarded the plaintiff $30,000 in damages.
The plaintiff had sought about $1 million in compensatory damages and over $50 million in punitive damages, 3M said.
In areas related to testing, manufacturing and packaging, the jury found 3M gave warnings to the plaintiff's plastic surgeon and did not commit any misrepresentation to the surgeon, the company said.
"We are extremely pleased by the verdict, which again confirms that silicone does not cause disease," Carol Ley, 3M associate medical director, said.
The trial lasted five weeks and was the twelfth decision in favor of the manufacturers involved in the revised class action settlement in the past 12 months, 3M said.
This was the second time since the beginning of 1996 that a jury has found in favor of 3M, it said.
